source.title: VeLO: Training Versatile Learned Optimizers by Scaling Up
source.authors: Luke Metz; James Harrison; C. Freeman; Amil Merchant; Lucas Beyer; James Bradbury; Naman Agrawal; B. Poole; Igor Mordatch; Adam Roberts; Jascha Narain Sohl-Dickstein

record.tranche_reason: The study reports held-out generalization results for learned-optimizer training, including a gradient-clipping change, but does not test a listed claim version directly.
record.gate_note: Most optimizer comparisons report training loss or optimization speed, not the training-to-test gap. The reported graph-network test-loss results bear on generalization but fit none of the listed versions. Values in Figure 25 are figure-only.
record.test_reason: The study evaluates a learned optimizer's optimization performance and selected held-out outcomes, but tests none of V1–V8. Its held-out optimizer comparisons lack an SGD comparator; its batch-size sweeps measure training loss rather than held-out performance. References to optimizer tuning and critical batch size do not establish tests of V4 or V5.
record.authors_conclusion: The record accurately paraphrases the materials-GNN finding: comparable training performance does not ensure comparable test performance, and maximum gradient-norm clipping at 1e-2 improves VeLO's generalization beyond Adam. The paper's broader conclusion concerns learned-optimizer versatility and optimization performance, with failures on some out-of-distribution tasks.
record.recipe_differences: The study trains models with a meta-learned optimizer and compares selected held-out results; it does not reproduce the listed study methods.
record.method_sensitivity: For the materials graph-network test-loss result, gradient clipping changes generalization; the text identifies maximum norm 1e-2 as the condition that improves generalization relative to Adam.

fits_no_version.finding: On materials-property prediction, VeLO achieves comparable training performance to Adam but worse test performance; clipping gradients to maximum norm 1e-2 improves generalization beyond Adam.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Gradient clipping can improve the held-out performance of a learned optimizer on an out-of-distribution graph-network task.

fits_no_version.finding: MLCommons validation comparisons favor VeLO on ViT and DeepSpeech, approximately match Adam on WMT17 and Conformer, and favor Adam substantially on ResNet50 (Section G.7).
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Held-out performance of VeLO relative to tuned Adam depends on the workload.

fits_no_version.finding: Fixed-example batch sweeps show a roughly tenfold larger critical batch size for VeLO on two small Transformers, with weaker or absent advantages on larger workloads.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: A learned optimizer can increase the critical batch size for training-loss optimization on some workloads.

record.problems: The graph-network test-loss evidence is shown in a figure without numerical values in the text. The reported result is for an out-of-distribution materials graph-network task, and the paper notes that performance on such tasks can be weak.
record.rows_left_out: No additional rows from the optimizer benchmark were included because those results report training loss or speed rather than the held-out generalization outcome relevant here.

untested.parts: Random-label fitting versus natural-label and random-label held-out accuracy under the same architecture and training recipe.
Held-out error when width increases beyond the width needed for zero training error. Figure 31 reports optimization loss after 10K iterations.
Controlled held-out comparisons of convolutional and fully connected image classifiers and the contribution of local connectivity.
Adaptive versus SGD or momentum-SGD held-out performance under limited or broader tuning. The SGD comparisons report training loss; the selected held-out comparisons use Adam versus VeLO.
Held-out performance across batch sizes at a fixed epoch budget, including recipe adaptations. The fixed-example batch sweeps report training loss.
Dropout's effect on held-out error, including small-data, excessive-dropout, and augmentation regimes.
Magnitude-aware sharpness and its correlation with generalization gaps relative to other measures.
Retraining after removing highly memorized examples versus equally many random examples.

record.verdict_notes: All three recorded rows concern the study's own optimizer comparison and belong under fits_no_version. Other held-out results in the text do not supply the comparisons required by a listed version, so they do not warrant version-specific missing entries or verdicts.

versions.untested_parts: Random-label memorization and natural-label held-out accuracy.
Test error as width passes the interpolation threshold.
Convolutional versus fully connected image-classifier test error and the stated architectural comparisons.
Held-out performance comparison of adaptive optimizers with SGD or momentum SGD under the specified tuning conditions.
Held-out performance under large batches with a fixed epoch budget and the specified recipe adaptations.
Dropout's effect on held-out error across the stated regimes.
Magnitude-aware sharpness and its relationship to the train-test gap.
Held-out accuracy after removing memorized examples.

rows.subject: Graph NN predicting chemical properties of materials
rows.note: Authors state that naive learned-optimizer training minimized training loss well but did not generalize well; the plotted Adam test-loss value is not specified in text.
rows.check: Adam's test-loss curve is a comparator for the study's learned optimizer, not evidence for any listed version. No numerical endpoint is readable from the supplied figure text.

rows.subject: Graph NN predicting chemical properties of materials
rows.operation_detail: Evaluate test loss with VeLO and gradient-norm clipping before input to the learned optimizer.
rows.note: Text says this clipping made the learned optimizers generalize better than Adam; the plotted test-loss value is not specified.
rows.check: Section F.4.5 explicitly identifies clipping at 1e-2 as fixing poor generalization, and Figure 25's caption reports performance better than Adam. This qualitative result is established, but it measures no listed version; 'observed' cannot describe a version-specific effect here.

rows.operation_detail: Evaluate test loss with VeLO and gradient-norm clipping before input to the learned optimizer.
rows.note: Figure 25 plots this clipping condition, but the text does not state its test-loss outcome separately.
